title: Minimum Masking and Shuffling Protections Against SPA
summary: The source warns against unprotected embedded software in side-channel-sensitive applications, while the minimum masking or shuffling protections and their implementation costs remain unresolved.

formal_statement.body: For embedded software implementations in applications sensitive to side-channel attacks, unprotected implementations should be avoided, while low-order masking and shuffling are potential countermeasures against $\mathrm{SPA}$. Determine concretely the minimum masking and shuffling protections needed to prevent $\mathrm{SPA}$ and measure their implementation costs, given the difficulty of protecting embedded software implementations.

scope.domain: Side-channel security of embedded software implementations in symmetric cryptography.
assumptions: The implementations are used in applications sensitive to side-channel attacks.
parameters: Masking and shuffling protections, as candidate countermeasures
Implementation costs, as the quantity to measure
scope.unresolved_remainder: Determine concretely the minimum masking and shuffling protections needed to prevent SPA and measure their implementation costs for embedded software implementations.

citations.label: Mode-Level vs. Implementation-Level Physical Security in Symmetric Cryptography: A Practical Guide Through the Leakage-Resistance Jungle

progress.summary: The source explicitly presents the concrete investigation of minimum protections and their implementation cost as an interesting open problem. It identifies low-order masking and shuffling as potential countermeasures for software implementations.
citation_labels: Davide Bellizia et al., Mode-Level vs. Implementation-Level Physical Security in Symmetric Cryptography: A Practical Guide Through the Leakage-Resistance Jungle
